name: Collision Check
purpose: Stop two sessions from building the same thing, or writing the same files, at the same time.
firesOn: BEFORE EACH WORK ITEM — not once per session. Also immediately before any merge.
_split_note: This is the READ half of what session-open C6 used to do alone. C6 stays the WRITE half. They were one step, which meant skipping it lost both — and gated the cheap self-interested act (looking) behind the expensive altruistic one (announcing).

_do_not_use.branch_list: 100+ branches, never deleted after merge. No way to tell live from long-dead.
_do_not_use.open_prs: 12 open on 2026-07-31, newest six days old, every one abandoned. Has the exact shape of a claim ledger and every entry is a lie. The first draft of this hook was built on it.

_primary_signal: githubmcp_list_commits with a path filter and since=today. Self-maintaining, timestamped, cannot go stale. Blind to work that has not landed yet — which is why the board is step 2 and the pre-merge re-check is step 4.
_halt_signals: create_branch returns 'Reference already exists' — another session named your work. NEVER adopt the branch.
merge_pull_request returns merge conflicts on a branch cut minutes ago
create_or_update_file returns 409 or a SHA mismatch
file content does not match the SHA being held
_origin: Third collision in a week. On 2026-07-31 two sessions built the batch-import feature simultaneously and it surfaced only at merge. C6 already mandated a presence post; neither session reached it. The one signal that fired before any work was wasted was a branch-name collision, and it was investigated and then explained away — the wrong question was asked of it (does this branch have content) instead of the right one (who made it and are they still working).
